sources.title: Deep learning for universal linear embeddings of nonlinear dynamics
sources.mechanism: An autoencoder learns coordinates with approximately linear evolution, trained with reconstruction, latent linearity and future prediction losses.
sources.supported_claim: Read section 3 (methods) and discussion: the learned-coordinate objective is established prior art; the continuous-spectrum extension also conditions evolution on an auxiliary frequency network.
limitations: Methods/discussion read, no reproduction. Uncontrolled smooth dynamical systems do not establish acquisition or compositional transfer for Noetloom's discrete action bank.
An encoder, linear transition and decoder alone are not a novelty claim.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Embed to Control: A Locally Linear Latent Dynamics Model for Control from Raw Images
sources.mechanism: A probabilistic encoder/decoder and state-dependent locally linear transition are trained with prediction/reconstruction and consistency between predicted and encoded next-state distributions.
sources.supported_claim: Read sections 2.3–2.4: the variational formulation uses a KL constraint to keep predicted latent states compatible with the representation used for repeated planning.
limitations: Methods read, no reproduction. The probabilistic control model differs from the deterministic finite-domain component probe.
Consistency is an established objective; its value here requires a matched behavioral comparison and cannot be inferred from the earlier GRU failure.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.14 GRUCell documentation
sources.mechanism: A gated recurrent cell with reset and update gates and a dense hidden transition; PyTorch applies the reset gate after the hidden affine transformation in its candidate activation.
sources.supported_claim: The documented equations, tensor shapes and default initialization define the direct control and its independent scalar implementation in EXP-0006.
limitations: API equations and shapes were read. This is implementation provenance, not evidence of acquisition, compositional generalization or architectural novelty.
sources.license_note: Documentation reference; using the already admitted PyTorch numerical dependency, no downloaded parameters or training data.

sources.title: Deep Sets
sources.mechanism: Apply a shared transform to set elements, aggregate by summation, and transform the result.
sources.supported_claim: Read sections 2.2 and 3.1: the shared-transform/sum architecture supplies permutation invariance. The countable-domain decomposition theorem and its stated fixed-size extension are prior art; the local audit derives its finite equivalence counts directly from Noetloom's code.
limitations: Methods/theorem statement review only; no reproduction or claim that every continuous set function is exactly represented at fixed finite capacity.
Permutation invariance does not establish new-computation generalization; finite-precision reductions can depend slightly on row order.
sources.license_note: Primary research reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
sources.mechanism: A context encoder and predictor learn to predict target image-block representations from an own-trained exponential-moving-average target encoder.
sources.supported_claim: Read sections 2–3, including targets, context, prediction and loss: prediction in representation space offers a training objective beyond a downstream answer label; masking and target construction constrain the problem.
limitations: The published method uses Vision Transformers; no architecture, weights or performance claim is adopted for Noetloom.
Methods review only, with no reproduction. This paper does not establish action-conditioned learning, unrestricted representation discovery or broad intelligence.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Relational inductive biases, deep learning, and graph networks
sources.mechanism: Explicit relational assumptions and shared computation constrain learning over structured inputs.
sources.supported_claim: Read the introduction and sections 2–2.1: fully connected, convolutional and recurrent layers embody different relational assumptions, sharing and invariances. Useful structure and learned parameters need not be opposing choices.
limitations: This is partly a position/review paper; architectural biases do not guarantee combinatorial generalization.
Graph-network implementation details and experimental claims were not reproduced; no fixed cognitive taxonomy is inferred.
sources.license_note: Primary conceptual reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
sources.mechanism: A recurrent state-space model learns action-conditioned latent dynamics alongside reconstruction and other prediction objectives.
sources.supported_claim: Read Learning algorithm / World model learning in the April 2024 preprint: observations shape latent state, past actions condition recurrent transitions, and reconstruction constrains predictive representations.
limitations: This read scope is the version-2 preprint, not a full review of the later Nature publication, actor/critic method or supplementary evaluation.
No reproduction performed. Control-task results do not establish Noetloom transfer, language capability or LLM displacement.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning
sources.mechanism: A learned processor imitates an algorithm in a latent space and is reused with learned input/output mappings.
sources.supported_claim: Read Algorithms in the real world and The blueprint of neural algorithmic reasoning: the proposed pipeline trains a processor with known-algorithm supervision, then fixes it while fitting encoders and decoders for natural inputs.
limitations: An opinion/blueprint article, not a general guarantee of extrapolation or autonomous procedure discovery.
No cited executor was reproduced; supervision and supplied algorithmic structure must remain explicit in any derived experiment.
sources.license_note: Primary conceptual reference only; no code, weights or datasets copied.

sources.title: Spatial Transformer Networks
sources.mechanism: An input-conditioned localization network predicts a transform whose differentiable sampler reorganizes a feature map before downstream computation.
sources.supported_claim: Read sections 3–3.4: the methods define learned transformation parameters, a sampling grid, differentiable interpolation, and training through downstream loss.
limitations: Methods review only; no reproduction or independent verification of the paper's experimental claims.
The transformation family and output grid remain designed; this does not establish unrestricted problem-representation discovery or a successor intelligence architecture.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, pretrained weights or data copied.

sources.title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention
sources.mechanism: Iterative competitive attention groups input features into exchangeable vectors with shared recurrent updates.
sources.supported_claim: Read sections 2–2.3 and 4–4.1: the authors define grouping, reconstruction and set-prediction uses, and evaluate object discovery against named baselines on synthetic scenes.
limitations: A supplied feature encoder, slot dimensionality and training objective constrain representation; findings do not establish arbitrary native formats.
The reported discovery table excludes one outlier in one setting; Noetloom retains all registered seeds.
No reproduction performed; EXP-0004 uses neither the full recurrent slot mechanism nor its datasets.
sources.license_note: Primary methods reference only; no code, pretrained weights or data copied.

sources.title: Neural Turing Machines
sources.mechanism: A differentiable neural controller reads and writes an external memory through attentional heads.
sources.supported_claim: The authors report preliminary demonstrations that NTMs learn simple copying, sorting, and associative-recall procedures from examples.
limitations: Methods and experiments sections 3–4.6 read: soft read/erase/add heads, cosine and location addressing, episodic resets, supervised binary objectives, and synthetic tasks. This review does not establish novelty or reproduce the paper's results.
The reported evidence is preliminary and concerns the paper's specified algorithmic tasks; broad general-purpose learning is not established by this source.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
sources.mechanism: Adaptive Computation Time learns how many recurrent steps to take between input and output.
sources.supported_claim: The paper reports that ACT adapts computation to task demands on four synthetic tasks; its character-level language-modeling experiment allocates more computation to harder-to-predict transitions but yields no large performance gain.
limitations: Read sections 2–2.2 and section 3 experimental setup: shared recurrent transitions, cumulative halting weights, ponder penalty, approximate gradients at discontinuities, and extensive time-penalty search with 20 initializations per value. EXP-0003 is a separate two-stage allocation probe, not a reproduction or implementation of ACT.
Evidence described here is limited to four synthetic tasks and one character-level Wikipedia language-modeling experiment.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
sources.mechanism: A wake-sleep loop grows a symbolic program language while training neural guidance on imagined and replayed problems.
sources.supported_claim: Read Wake/Sleep Program Learning (wake, abstraction and dreaming) and the opening Results for list processing and text editing: learned library abstractions compress discovered programs while a recognition model guides search over a supplied initial vocabulary.
limitations: Method review and reported examples, not an independent reproduction or a full review of the supplementary algorithm.
Typed program representations, initial primitives, search and task likelihoods are supplied; general open-ended skill acquisition and Noetloom novelty are not established.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Zoology: Measuring and Improving Recall in Efficient Language Models
sources.mechanism: The study compares attention and gated-convolution recall, introduces multi-query associative recall, and evaluates sparse-attention hybrids.
sources.supported_claim: Across 17 pretrained models, the authors attribute much of the Pile perplexity gap to in-context associative recall; evaluated input-dependent sparse-attention hybrids close 97.4% of that gap while retaining sub-quadratic scaling.
limitations: Read sections 3.2, 4.3 and appendix E: multi-query distances and working-set shifts; synthetic runs use 100,000 training and 3,000 evaluation examples, 64 epochs and an AdamW learning-rate sweep. EXP-0002 is a smaller independent diagnostic, not a reproduction.
The reported findings are about the tested language models, Pile comparison, and associative-recall analyses; they do not establish universal superiority of a hybrid architecture.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
sources.mechanism: A learned neural long-term memory stores historical context alongside attention over current context; the paper presents three architecture variants.
sources.supported_claim: The authors report results on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, genomics, and time series, including higher needle-in-a-haystack accuracy than baselines beyond two million context tokens.
limitations: Claims reflect the paper's evaluated tasks and baselines; deployment cost, continual weight learning, and general-purpose memory are not established by this source.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
sources.mechanism: A recurrent block is iterated at inference to scale computation through latent-space reasoning without generating additional reasoning tokens.
sources.supported_claim: The authors report a proof-of-concept model trained at 3.5 billion parameters on 800 billion tokens that improves on reasoning benchmarks as test-time computation increases.
limitations: The source describes a proof of concept and benchmark results; broad task coverage and production-scale advantages are not established.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
sources.mechanism: A shared recursive Transformer stack uses routers to assign per-token recursion depth and compute attention among still-active tokens.
sources.supported_claim: For evaluated models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, the authors report lower validation perplexity, better few-shot accuracy, and higher throughput than specified vanilla and recursive baselines at equal training FLOPs.
limitations: The abstract bounds experiments to the stated model scales and baselines; scaling beyond them is not established by this source.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.

sources.title: Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning
sources.mechanism: Continual backpropagation maintains network plasticity by randomly reinitializing a small fraction of less-used units over training.
sources.supported_claim: The authors report that standard deep-learning methods lose plasticity in tested continual-learning settings, while continual backpropagation maintained it in their supervised and reinforcement-learning experiments.
limitations: The reported settings include ImageNet-derived and reinforcement-learning tasks; large-language-model continual learning is not established by this source.
sources.license_note: Reference only; code, weights, and data licenses require separate review before reuse.
